description:
FILED s543u (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28) by member 4 (the rule-12 read of the escape rewriter against perlre / perlrebackslash).

THE SHAPE (perl 5.40.3 vs the s543u tree):
    print "ab" =~ /(?|(a)|(b))\1/ ? "y" : "n", "\n";     # perl n
    print "ab" =~ /(?|(a)|(c))b/ ? "y[$&] [$1]" : "n", "\n";  # perl y[ab] [a]
    PCL: both die "Character '|' may not follow '(?' in regex" (trappable, one line).

LOUD, not silent: the pattern refuses to compile.  A fix: in the parse tree (%pcl-mark-tree's renumbering), give each alternative of the group the same register numbers -- cl-ppcre numbers registers in tree order, so the alternatives' registers must be remapped onto the first alternative's, and the scanner wrapper (%pcl-keep-scanner's compaction) must merge them.  Listed in docs/not-supported.md ns-regex-escapes.
frequency_reason: no Rosetta program, board dist, everyday program or lib/ shim holds `(?|` (grepped s543u); perlre documents it
subject: LOUD: a branch-reset group `(?|...)` dies at the compile with cl-ppcre's "Character '|' may not follow '(?'" where perl numbers each alternative's groups from the same number
triage_reason: perlre "Extended Patterns"; within reach of a rewrite that renumbers (the s543u keep registers already renumber back-references in the parse tree)
